en.name: Baba ganoush
en.summary: Home-made baba ganoush keeps 5–7 days in the refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. No authority publishes a figure for it — treat it like hummus made without preservatives, which is the closest thing there is: same tahini, garlic and lemon base, same absence of anything to preserve it.
en.pantry: This is not a counter food. Baba ganoush is a cooked vegetable purée with raw garlic and lemon stirred through it and no preservative at all — a moist, low-acid, ready-to-eat dip, which is exactly the profile that gets contaminated after cooking and has no further cooking step to fall back on. Serve it from a bowl for the length of a meal and put the rest away: no more than two hours out of the fridge, and no more than one hour if the room is above 32 °C (90 °F). Do not leave a bowl on a summer table all afternoon.
en.fridge: A sealed tub at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, 5–7 days. It is a fresh, unpasteurised dip with no preservatives, so it behaves like homemade hummus: bacteria and yeasts start working the moment it is made. Pour a film of olive oil over the surface to stop it browning, and use a clean spoon rather than dipping bread into the tub. Weeping liquid is normal: pour it off and stir. Commercially made, pasteurised baba ganoush behaves differently and should be judged by its printed date until you open it, then given the same 5–7 days.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for baba ganoush. It does freeze acceptably and thaws watery, because aubergine flesh is mostly water and the ice crystals break it down — drain the liquid off and re-whip it with a little more tahini and oil and it comes back well enough for cooking or for a rough dip, though not for a smooth one. Freeze it before the garnish goes on, in small portions, and do not refreeze.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight, pour off the water it has released, and beat it back together with a little tahini and olive oil. Never thaw it on the counter.
spoilage: A fizzy taste or a yeasty smell — it is fermenting and should go.
Mould at the surface or around the rim of the tub.
A sour or sharp smell instead of smoky aubergine, tahini and lemon.
A slimy or stringy texture, or liquid that will not stir back in.
tips: Keep a film of olive oil over the surface to stop it browning.
Serve a portion in a bowl rather than putting the storage tub on the table.
Use a clean spoon every time; never dip bread straight into the tub.
Label the tub with the date it was made.

faq.q: How long does baba ganoush keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 5–7 days in a sealed tub at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. That figure is borrowed from preservative-free hummus rather than published for baba ganoush.
There is no published limit. It freezes acceptably but thaws watery — drain it and re-whip it, and use it in cooking rather than as a smooth dip.

faq.q: Why is there liquid on top of my baba ganoush?
faq.a: Aubergine releases water as it stands. Pour it off and stir. A fizzy taste or yeasty smell is different, and means it is fermenting.

zh.name: 中東烤茄泥（baba ganoush）
zh.summary: 自製的中東烤茄泥在 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 5～7 天。沒有任何單位為它公布過期限——請把它比照「沒有添加防腐劑的鷹嘴豆泥」來看，那是最接近的東西：一樣的芝麻醬、大蒜與檸檬基底，一樣什麼防腐的東西都沒有。
zh.pantry: 這不是可以放在檯面上的食物。烤茄泥是煮熟的蔬菜泥，拌進生蒜和檸檬，完全沒有防腐劑——一份含水、低酸、即食的沾醬，正是那種「煮完之後才被污染」而且後面再也沒有加熱步驟可以補救的類型。一頓飯的時間內從碗裡取用沒問題，吃完就收起來：離開冰箱不超過兩小時，室溫超過 32 °C 時不超過一小時。不要讓一碗茄泥在夏天的餐桌上放一整個下午。
zh.fridge: 密封盒放 4 °C 以下，5～7 天。它是未殺菌、不加防腐劑的新鮮沾醬，表現和自製鷹嘴豆泥一樣：做好的那一刻，細菌和酵母就開始工作了。表面淋一層橄欖油防止褐變，取用時用乾淨的湯匙，不要拿麵包直接往盒子裡沾。出水是正常的：倒掉再拌勻即可。市售經過殺菌的烤茄泥不一樣，未開封請以包裝日期為準，開封後同樣抓 5～7 天。
zh.freezer: 烤茄泥沒有冷凍期限。它冷凍起來還算可以，但解凍會出很多水，因為茄子肉幾乎都是水，冰晶會把組織撐破——把水倒掉，再加一點芝麻醬和油重新打勻，拿去入菜或當口感粗一點的沾醬沒問題，但回不到細滑的狀態。請在還沒加配料之前分小份冷凍，而且不要二次冷凍。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍，倒掉滲出的水，再加一點芝麻醬與橄欖油重新拌勻。不要放室溫退冰。
spoilage: 吃起來有氣泡感或聞起來有酵母味——它在發酵，該丟了。
聞起來發酸刺鼻，而不是煙燻茄子、芝麻醬與檸檬的味道。
質地變黏滑或牽絲，或滲出的水怎麼拌都拌不回去。
tips: 表面保持一層橄欖油，防止褐變。
分一小碗上桌，不要把保存盒直接端上餐桌。
每次都用乾淨湯匙，不要拿麵包直接沾盒子。

faq.q: 烤茄泥冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封盒放 4 °C 以下 5～7 天。這個數字是比照無防腐劑的鷹嘴豆泥，不是為烤茄泥公布的。
沒有公布的期限。冷凍還算可行，但解凍會出水——瀝掉後重新打勻，用在烹調而不是當細滑沾醬。

faq.q: 上面積了一層水正常嗎？
faq.a: 正常，茄子放久會出水，倒掉拌勻即可。但如果吃起來有氣泡感或有酵母味，那是在發酵，情況不同。
